Judgment

1. This memorandum of Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the MV Act') assailing the award passed by the learned Motor Accidents Claims BRMR,J Tribunal (III Additional District Judge) (Fast Track Court), Khammam (for short 'the Tribunal') in MATOP.No.1155 of 2004, dated 26.07.2011.
2. Appellant is the respondent No.2, respondent No.1 is the petitioner and respondent No.2 is the respondent No.1 in the O.P.
United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Shaik Nagul Meera And Another on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158995769/
1

entities.label: COURT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Respondent No.1 - petitioner has filed claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the date of the accident till the date of realization against respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.

4. On 20.06.2004 at about 09.50 p.m., respondent No.1 - petitioner along with his friend Mohan went to Mamillagudem on their work and were returning on a motor cycle bearing No.AP-20-G-2477, when they reached daily needs centre, one motor cycle bearing No.AP-37-G-4226, which is driven by respondent No.2 - respondent No.1 in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident, due to which respondent No.1 - petitioner sustained injuries.
On the complaint PS Traffic, Khammam registered a case in Crime No.111 of 2004 for the offence under Section 337 of IPC against the driver of the crime vehicle and filed charge sheet.

Respondent No.1 - petitioner has took treatment with Dr.T.Madhan Singh, Orthopedic Surgeon as inpatient for a period of 30 days, he was aged about 28 years as on the date of accident, doing real estate business and earning Rs.5,000/- per month.
BRMR,J 5.
Respondent No.2 - respondent No.1 did not file any counter.
Appellant - respondent No.2 has filed counter and denied the manner in which the accident has taken place.
6. Respondent No.1 - petitioner is examined as PW1, also examined PW2 - Dr.T.Madhan Singh and got marked Exs.A1 to A8.
Appellant - respondent No.2 has got examined RW1 - M.Radha Krishna and got marked Ex.B1- C.C. of Insurance Policy.

7. The learned Tribunal after going through the evidence adduced by the parties coupled with the documents marked thereon has awarded compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till the date of deposit of the amount against respondent Nos.1 and 2 jointly and severally.

8. Learned counsel for the appellant - respondent No.2 [Insurance Company] submits that the Tribunal ought to have exonerated the appellant - respondent No.2 from the liability in paying the compensation as the police has filed charge sheet against the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.AP-37-G-4226 as he was not possessing valid driving licence as on the date of accident and owner (respondent No.2 herein) did not contest the matter.

The learned Tribunal has erroneous fastened the liability on the appellant - respondent No.2 on the ground that the insurance company did not examine the rider of the motor cycle BRMR,J of respondent No.2 - respondent No.1 or the RTO in order to prove that the accused driver did not possess valid driving licence and prayed to allow the appeal.

9. Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 - petitioner submits that though the respondent No.1 - petitioner has not filed appeal seeking enhancement of compensation but he is entitled for just compensation.
The Tribunal has wrongly taken the income of the respondent No.1 - petitioner at Rs.3,000/- per month, which has to be taken at Rs.4,500/- per month.

Counsel to substantiate his contention has relied on the decisions in the cases of (i) Ramachandrappa Vs. Manager, Royal United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Shaik Nagul Meera And Another on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158995769/
2

sentences.text: 10. Respondent No.2 - respondent No.1 failed to advance his arguments in spite of granting opportunity.

11. Heard learned counsel and perused the material on record.
12.

Now the points for consideration are:
(2011) 13 SCC 236 2012 ACJ 191 2020 ACJ 2156 BRMR,J i) Whether the learned Tribunal has awarded just compensation to the respondent No.1 - petitioner?
ii) Whether the award passed by the learned Tribunal suffers from any perversity or illegality, if so, does it require interference of this Court?
13.

The learned Tribunal while discussing Ex.A2 - C.C of charge sheet observed in paragraph No.21 as under:
"21.

As per the above contention of R-2 that under Ex.A2 police filed charge sheet U/sec. 3, 181 r/w 177 of M.V.Act that the driver of crime vehicle did not possess driving licence at the time of accident.
But to prove the same R-2 did not examine Mohan who is said to be the rider of motor cycle on which the claim petitioner was travelling at the time of accident to prove the same.

Further they did not even examine R-1/owner or driver of crime vehicle or any person from RTO Office to prove that the driver of crime vehicle did not possess valid driving licence at the time of accident and moreover mere allegation in the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to establish that the driver of crime vehicle did not possess driving licence at the time of accident.
So, in absence of such evidence the above contention of R-2 does not appears to be having force.
As per Ex.B1-Insurance policy, the policy is in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, R-1 and R-2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation awarded to the claim petitioner.
Hence, I held this issue accordingly."

14. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under different heads is as under:
 Sl.No. Name of the Head Compensation  awarded by the  Tribunal  1. Towards Pain and suffering Rs.30,000/-

3  2. Towards Disability Rs.50,000/-
 3.

sentences.text:
Medical and Hospital Bills Rs.34,000/-
 4. Towards loss of income during the  period of treatment by considering  the income of Rs.3,000/- per  month Rs.3,000 x 2 months =
 Rs.6,000/- Rs.6,000/-
 5.

Towards attendance,
 transportation, Extra  nourishment Rs.5,000/-
 Total Rs.1,25,000/-
15.
In Ramachandrappa1 the Supreme Court has taken the earning of a Coolie as Rs.4,500/- per month wherein the accident has taken place in the year 2004.

In the present case, accident has also taken place in the year 2004 but the learned Tribunal has taken the income of respondent No.1 - petitioner at Rs.3,000/- per month, which is on lower side and this Court takes the income of the respondent No.1 - petitioner as Rs.4,500/- per month for calculating the compensation.

16. The age of the respondent No.1 - petitioner is shown as 28 years in the claim petition, the same age is mentioned in Ex.A3 - C.C. of disability certificate and Ex.A8 - C.C. of medical certificate.
The Tribunal has not taken into consideration the age of the respondent No.1 - petitioner while calculating the disability.

17. PW2 - Dr.T.Madhan Singh deposed that he is working as Civil Orthopedic surgeon, Government Hospital, Khammam, and practicing in BRMR,J Tarun Orthopedi Trama Care Hospital, Wyra Raod,
Khammam, the patient by name Sk.Nagulmeera aged 28 years was admitted in Tarun Orthopedic Hospital on 25.06.2004 with fracture right hip joint, he has examined him, conducted surgery on 27.06.2004 by inserting plate and he was discharged on 09.07.2004.

entities.text: BRMR,J Tarun Orthopedi Trama Care Hospital, Wyra Raod
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has issued receipts for Rs.20,000/- and discharge summary, he also issued Ex.A3 - disability certificate showing the disability at 25 to 30% and there is a shortening in right leg (1/2) which is permanent in nature.
Disability certificate is Ex.A3 and the patient require another operation for removal of plate, which may cost about Rs.20,000/-.
18. The learned Tribunal has awarded a lump sum amount of Rs.50,000/- towards disability.
In view of the evidence of PW2 and the decision of the Supreme Court in Pappu Deo Yadav Vs. Naresh Kumar 4, this Court fixes the disability of the respondent No.1 - petitioner at 10%.

entities.text: Pappu Deo Yadav Vs. Naresh Kumar 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal has taken two months loss of income and this Court is not interfering with the same.
As per Ex.A8 - C.C. of medical certificate respondent No.1 - petitioner has sustained one grievous injury.

19. The learned Tribunal has lost sight of Ex.A2 - C.C. of charge sheet, which goes to show that it is filed against respondent No.2 - respondent AIR 2020 SC 4424 BRMR,J No.1 under Sections 3, 188 r/w 177 MV Act and under Section 338 of IPC.
The charge sheet goes to show that respondent No.2 - respondent No.1 is not possessing valid driving license as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: 4 Tribunal has wrongly arrived at a conclusion that the appellant - respondent No.2 has not examined the rider of the crime vehicle.
The said conclusion requires interference of this Court and the same is liable to be set aside.

20. Appellant - respondent No.2 being the insurer of the crime vehicle, is liable to pay the compensation arrived by this Court and recover the amount from respondent No.2 - respondent No.1.
21.
Respondent No.1 - petitioner is entitled for just compensation.

See: Laxman2 and Surekha3.
22.
The income of the respondent No.1 - petitioner is taken at Rs.4,500/- per month and annual income comes to Rs.54,000/- (4,500 x 12).

As the respondent No.1 - petitioner is aged about 28 years as on the date of accident, the appropriate multiplier is '17' as per Smt. Sarla Verma & Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.
5, which comes to Rs.9,18,000/- (54,000 x 17).

sentences.text: If 10% disability is taken, then the loss of income due to disability would be Rs.91,800/- (9,18,000 x 10%).

The calculation arrived by this Court is as under:

 Rounded off to  Rs.35,000/-
 4. Loss of income due to Rs.91,800/-
 disability  5. Loss of earning Rs.9,000/-
 (for two months) 4,500 x 2 6.

Transportation charges, Extra Rs.15,000/-
nourishment and Attendant charges (Rs.5,000/- each) Total Rs.2,10,800/-
24.

The learned Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum, which has to be enhanced to 9% as per the decision in the case of Anjali and Others vs. Lokendra Rathod and others 6.
25.
